documents.name: AI Addendum
documents.title: AI Addendum
documents.summary: AI-specific terms to add to a product agreement: who owns the input and output, and whether the provider may train on them.
aliases: can they train on our data
documents.attachment: An AI Addendum layers onto a product agreement you already have; it adds AI terms rather than replacing that agreement.

fields.name: Provider
fields.label: the company providing the AI features

fields.name: Customer
fields.label: the company using them

fields.name: Training Data
fields.label: what data, if any, the provider may train on
fields.hint: Leave this out and the provider may not train on your input or output at all, which is the standard terms' default.

fields.name: Training Purposes
fields.label: what the provider may train for
fields.hint: Only meaningful if training is permitted above.

fields.name: Training Restrictions
fields.label: any limits on that training

fields.name: Improvement Restrictions
fields.label: any limits on using input and output to improve the service

documents.name: Business Associate Agreement

documents.summary: A HIPAA agreement covering how a vendor may handle protected health information on a covered entity's behalf.
documents.attachment: A BAA supplements an existing agreement between the two companies rather than standing on its own.

fields.name: Provider
fields.label: the business associate handling the health information

fields.name: Company
fields.label: the covered entity whose health information it is

fields.name: BAA Effective Date
fields.label: the date this BAA starts

fields.name: Breach Notification Period
fields.label: how quickly a breach must be reported
fields.hint: A period, such as '5 business days' or '72 hours'.

fields.name: Agreement
fields.label: the agreement this BAA attaches to

fields.hint: Leave this out and no extra limits apply beyond the standard terms.

documents.name: Data Processing Agreement
documents.title: Data Processing Agreement
documents.summary: A GDPR data processing agreement covering how a vendor processes personal data on a customer's behalf, including transfers out of the EEA.
documents.attachment: A DPA supplements the main agreement between the two companies rather than standing on its own.

fields.name: Provider
fields.label: the company processing the data

fields.name: Customer
fields.label: the company whose data it is

fields.name: Agreement
fields.label: the agreement this DPA attaches to
fields.hint: The name and date of the underlying contract between the two companies.

fields.name: Categories of Personal Data
fields.label: what kinds of personal data are processed
fields.hint: Such as names, email addresses, IP addresses, usage records.

fields.name: Categories of Data Subjects
fields.label: whose personal data it is
fields.hint: Such as the customer's employees, its end users, or its own customers.

fields.name: Nature and Purpose of Processing
fields.label: what the processing is for

fields.name: Duration of Processing
fields.label: how long the data is processed for
fields.hint: Commonly 'for the term of the Agreement, plus any retention period'.

fields.name: Approved Subprocessors
fields.label: which subprocessors are approved
fields.hint: For each one, its name, the country it operates in, and what it does. List them all in one answer.

fields.name: Provider Security Contact
fields.label: who to contact about a security incident
fields.hint: An email address reaches someone quickly enough to matter here.

fields.name: Security Policy
fields.label: the security policy that applies
fields.hint: Name it or link to it.

fields.name: Governing Member State
fields.label: the EU member state whose law governs the transfer clauses
fields.hint: Such as Ireland or Germany. Only relevant if personal data leaves the EEA.

fields.name: Frequency of Transfer
fields.label: how often data is transferred
fields.hint: Such as 'continuous' or 'monthly batch export'.

fields.name: Special Category Data
fields.label: any special category data involved
fields.hint: Health, biometric, racial or ethnic origin, political opinions, and the like. Leave it out if none is processed.

fields.name: Special Category Data Restrictions or Safeguards
fields.label: the extra safeguards for that special category data

documents.name: Service Level Agreement
documents.title: Service Level Agreement
documents.summary: Uptime and response-time commitments for a cloud service, and the service credits owed when they are missed.
documents.attachment: An SLA attaches to a Cloud Service Agreement. The customer, provider and subscription period are defined by that agreement, and are repeated here so the document reads on its own.

fields.name: Provider
fields.label: the company providing the service

fields.name: Customer
fields.label: the customer it is promised to

fields.name: Target Uptime
fields.label: the uptime you are committing to
fields.hint: A percentage, such as '99.9%'.

fields.name: Subscription Period
fields.label: the subscription period these levels are measured over
fields.hint: This comes from the Cloud Service Agreement, such as '12 months from the Order Date'.

fields.name: Target Response Time
fields.label: how quickly support will respond
fields.hint: A time, such as '4 business hours'.

fields.name: Support Channel
fields.label: how customers reach support
fields.hint: An email address, portal, or phone number.

fields.name: Uptime Credit
fields.label: the credit owed when uptime is missed
fields.hint: Often a tier list, such as '10% of monthly fees below 99.9%, 25% below 99%'. Describe it in your own words.

fields.name: Response Time Credit
fields.label: the credit owed when response times are missed

fields.name: Scheduled Downtime
fields.label: maintenance windows that do not count against uptime
fields.hint: Such as 'Sundays 02:00-06:00 UTC, with 48 hours notice'.
